item.title: Human-in-the-Loop Intelligent Automation: A Review of Trust, Oversight, and Workforce Implications
item.description:
[预印本] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
Intelligent automation is now used to retrieve information, predict, recommend, generate content, route workflows and take physical or administrative action. Human-in-the-loop (HITL) design is often suggested as a possible fail-safe but it does not necessarily mean that a person is always in control. Oversight can be undermined by lack of time, authority, competence, independent evidence, or feedback or by a lack of real accountability despite the title of oversight. In this paper we explore HITL intelligent automation from three intertwined perspectives: calibrated trust, operational oversight, and workforce implications. It combines existing human-automation research, guidance for human–AI interaction, risk-management standards, regulation, and evidence of labor. A threat model encompasses technical misfortune, adversarial manipulation, cognitive and organizational failure, and harmful deployment of workforce. The mathematical formulation determines the automation modes based on expected error consequence, uncertainty, review cost, workload and skill preservation. The suggested architecture is that of separating the execution of the model from the risk routing, human decision making, dual authorization, audit, appeal, and learning feedback. A seeded synthetic experiment with 10,000 binary decisions is conducted for the comparisons between automation-only, passive universal review, risk-adaptive HITL, and dual control. With the declared generator, adaptive review achieves a 83.6% to 85.0% accuracy rate, while reviewing 37.1% of cases, and dual control achieves a 87.0% accuracy rate with a 5.2% rate of high impact error. These are indicative values and not measurements taken in the workplace. The review finds that effective HITL systems must have meaningful intervention capability, calibrated reliance, representative evaluation, protected worker voice, continuous competence and evidence of oversight functioning under realistic workload and failure.

従来の選挙競争に関する統計力学的モデルは、一般に二値イジングスピン仕様($s_{i}\in\{+1,-1\}$)に依拠しているが、これは一定の投票参加恒等式($s_{i}^{2}\equiv1$)を課すものであり、外生的な政策ショックや評判ショックが直接的なイデオロギーの転向のみを通じて選挙結果を変化させることを前提としている。この制約を緩和し、有権者の戦略的棄権($s_{i}=0$)を内生化するため、本研究では米国50州の空間ネットワーク上に、多項ロジット型量子応答均衡(QRE)と結合した3状態スピン1 Blume–Capel選挙ポテンシャルゲームを定式化する。各州において、有権者は非妥協的な党派的コア層と、反応性を有する3つの社会経済的階層(労働者階級および企業同調層の有権者、制度的エスタブリッシュメント層の有権者、ならびに真実追求型の無党派有権者)に分割される。水平磁場は、縦断的な世論調査および抗議活動の時系列データ(2024年12月〜2026年10月)から較正された純党派的政策格差を捉え、結晶場は純粋な市民参加インセンティブから多争点にわたる制度的シニシズムを差し引いたものを表す。解析的な6次ランダウ自由エネルギー展開により、中間選挙後の立法府の膠着状態と多争点政策ショックによってある階層の結晶場が対称三重臨界スピノーダル閾値($D_{t}/J_{\mathrm{eff}}=-\ln(4)/3\approx-0.4621$)を下回ると、2次および4次のランダウ係数の符号が反転し($a_{2}>0, a_{4}<0$)、磁化ゼロにおける常磁性的な棄権のポテンシャル井戸が安定化することが示される。大規模なベクトル化モンテカルロ・シミュレーション(24の歴史的および反事実的レジームにわたり、各レジームあたり$1.0\times10^{6}$から$1.2\times10^{6}$試行)により、交差圧力に晒された階層における選択的棄権が、純党派磁化の分子($m$)よりも速く有効投票率の分母($q$)を縮小させ、直接的な党派的離反を伴うことなく実効厳密な4次ビンダー・キュムラント分解($U_{4,k}$)および1次ソボル感度指数($S_{1,k}(X_{0})<10^{-5}$)により、初期事前分布に対する不変性が検証されるとともに、非対称的な投票ロックインと3階層全体の参加崩壊とを隔てる相境界が特定される。 Intelligence)エージェント群(Swarm)の実戦投入によって根底から崩壊した。脱獄(jailbreak)されたオープンウェイトモデルとオープンソースのエージェント・ハーネスを結合させることで、偵察、ゼロデイ脆弱性の発見、および多段階の侵入プロセスは完全に自動化され、企業1社あたりの侵害限界費用は約50〜100ドルという極小水準にまで低下している。実際に、複数の商用・オープンモデル(Claude、Grok、Kimi、および改変されたPentestGPT基盤等)を並行稼働させ、認可されたレッドチーム演習を装うことで安全ガードレールを突破し、中南米の銀行・金融機関400社以上やアルゼンチンの医療機関少なくとも15組織に自動侵入した事案や、インターネット上に公開されたAIゲートウェイおよびModel October」)にスーパーエージェント主導の脆弱性カスケードとして顕在化した。世界のWebバックエンドの約70%を支えるPHPにおいて、数十年間潜在していた致命的な遠隔コード実行(RCE)脆弱性(CVE-2026-109618およびCVE-2026-109619、通称「PHP2Shell」、CVSS 9.2、ならびに後続のCVE-2026-115560)がAI支援のソースコード監査によって露呈すると、公開直後に数百万件規模の自動悪用試行が発生し、ペイロードをリアルタイムに変異させる攻撃によって、日本の地方銀行約20行や英国の32の行政サービスをはじめとする世界中のシステムが緊急停止(ロックダウン)を余儀なくされた。さらに同時期に、Node.js(CVE-2026-111497、「Node2Shell」)、JavaおよびGraalVM(CVE-2026-91403、CVSS Chase、Bank of America、Citigroup、Morgan Stanley、Wells Fargoなどの主要銀行において、利用者が利便性のためにID・パスワードを共有した未承認のサードパーティ製AIエージェントが口座内で本人の指示と無関係な資金移動等を試みる挙動が相次いで検知された。本人が認証情報を渡しているため不正アクセスとの識別が困難であり、各行は外部エージェントの遮断や口座の「読み取り専用(read-only)化」による防御を迫られているが、これは「資金が盗まれなくとも、防御側自らが送金・決済機能を停止させることで金融システムの信用と流動性が崩壊する」という国際通貨基金(IMF)の警告が現実化したパラドックスを示している。 さらに重大な戦略的脅威は、これらの事象が核兵器による物理的破壊以上に長期間にわたり社会基盤を蝕む「情報的不衛生状態(prolonged informational unsanitariness:認識論的・生体的・暗号学的汚染)」をもたらしている点である。物理的インフラは再建可能であり、漏洩したパスワードはリセット可能であるが、インターネットの信頼の根幹をなす暗号基盤の腐食と、変更不可能な生体・医療・身分証明データの流出は不可逆的な汚染を引き起こす。具体的には、インドの認証局eMudhraにおいて秘密鍵が極めて容易に算出可能な8枚の中間証明書が発行されていた問題(同社は世界向けのSSL/TLS証明書事業から撤退し、主要ブラウザによるルート証明書の信頼停止やPythonパッケージ管理環境 `pip`、`certifi` およびコンテナイメージの緊急更新を招いた)は、オンライン上の真正性検証基盤そのものが汚染され得ることを実証した。これと並行して、米国成人の約3分の1および病院の半数にサービスを提供する医療検査大手Quest Diagnosticsの患者記録システム(Quanum)への侵入、カリフォルニア州の公立学校生徒570万人分のデータ流出、日本国内における佐川急便の配送データ(最大約5,323万件)、パーク24「タイムズカー」の暗号化された運転免許証画像(約146万件に外部送信痕跡)、デジタル庁や地方自治体が利用する委託先Web・メール配信システム(Studio、ブラストメール等)、パナソニック子会社における社内規定違反の外部生成AI送信による33万4,000人分の個人情報漏洩、さらには海運IT企業を踏み台とした18カ国40以上の港湾・海運組織へのランサムウェア侵害(n0n)など、リセット不可能な実空間データの流出が常態化している。これらの汚染データは、SNS上の資産情報と結合されることで、暗号資産保有者への物理的拉致・強迫(レンチ攻撃)や匿名・流動型犯罪グループ(トクリュウ)による家族ぐるみの強盗・詐欺の標的リストへと転用され、サイバー空間の脆弱性が物理的な治安崩壊へと直結している。 このような環境下において、攻撃者は中国やロシア等に対するジオブロッキングを回避するため、欧米の正規トラフィックに紛れるクラウドIPや高性能VPS、匿名化プロキシを経由して攻撃を実行しており、送信元IPログのみに基づく帰属特定(Attribution)や一国単独での境界防御は構造的に機能不全に陥っている。最先端AIによる形式検証(ClaudeとRocqを 결합し123のオープンソースライブラリに対して数億行の機械検証済み数学的証明を生成・自動パッチ化する技術等)や、静止軌道衛星を用いた主権エアギャップ通信網、国家計算備蓄(National Compute Reserves)の構築は重要な防衛手段であるものの、技術的対策のみでは「1回あたり数十ドルで無限に反復される自動攻撃」との消耗戦を終わらせることはできない。サイバー犯罪の収益構造を断ち切り、報復の連鎖による世界的なインターネットのロックダウンや金融決済網の凍結、ひいては核保有国間の全面的なハイブリッド戦争へのエスカレーションを回避するためには、国境を越えた資金追跡・没収とAIエージェントの統治に関する国際的枠組みが不可欠となる。これこそが、本研究の3状態スピン1 Blume–Capel選挙ポテンシャルゲームにおいて、巨大な人口・データ空間・計算資源を抱える超大国3国(米国・中国・ロシア)およびBRICS諸国との間で、イデオロギー的対立を超えた危機管理上のコンセンサスや限定的・条件付きの戦略的譲歩による連携シナリオ(外生ショック $\xi_{\mathrm{trilat}} \sim \mathrm{Gamma}(2.8, 0.24)$)が想定される論理的必然性である。モデル内において、この超国家的生存戦略は高い戦略的不可逆性パラメータ($\Omega_{\mathrm{strat}} \in [2.20, 2.25]$)を伴う制度的グリッドロック指数 $$G_{\mathrm{inst}}(t) = \Omega_{\mathrm{strat}}\left(0.45\,I_{\mathrm{House}}(t) + 0.55\,I_{\mathrm{Senate}}(t)\right)$$ として定式化される。この不可逆的な大国間調整は、労働者階級・企業連携層($w_{\mathrm{work},k}$)のうち企業・エネルギー派閥($\phi_{\mathrm{corp},k} w_{\mathrm{work},k}$)にはインフラ・資源取引の安定をもたらす一方で、伝統的な「米国第一主義」を信奉するポピュリスト・ナショナリスト派閥($(1-\phi_{\mathrm{corp},k}) w_{\mathrm{work},k}$)には、裏切り閾値 $\tau_{\mathrm{betray}}$ を超えた際に非線形の認知的不協和ペナルティ $$\Psi_{\mathrm{diss}}(\xi_{\mathrm{trilat}}) = \gamma_{\mathrm{diss}}\max\left(0, \xi_{\mathrm{trilat}} - \tau_{\mathrm{betray}}\right)^2$$ を発生させる。そして、2026年中間選挙後の両院ねじれ($G_{\mathrm{inst}}^{2026} = 2.20\text{--}2.25$)および多段階のスキャンダル文書開示($\Lambda_{\mathrm{leak}} \in [0.03, 1.00]$)と結合することで、エスタブリッシュメント層($c=\mathrm{est}$)や無党派層($c=\mathrm{truth}$)、さらには特定条件下での労働者層の結晶場 $D_{c,k} = B_{\mathrm{duty},c,k} - C_{\mathrm{vote},c,k}$ を普遍的三重臨界スピノーダル閾値 $D_t/J_{\mathrm{eff}} = -\ln(4)/3 \approx -0.4621$ 未満へと侵食させ、有権者の大規模な戦略的棄権カスケード($s_i = 0$)とマクロな選挙相分岐を引き起こすのである。 For three decades, the architecture of global cybersecurity rested upon an implicit economic premise: because human operators possessed finite time and cognitive bandwidth, adversarial intrusions were naturally bounded by the opportunity cost of target selection. The operational deployment of autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) and synthetic intelligence (SI) agent swarms has dismantled this scarcity constraint, reducing the marginal cost of automated reconnaissance, zero-day vulnerability discovery, and multi-stage exploitation to negligible levels—empirically estimated at approximately $50 to $100 per compromised enterprise when utilizing jailbroken open-weight models coupled with open-source agentic harnesses. Threat intelligence observations confirm that criminal syndicates have parallelized commercial and open-weight models (including Claude, Grok, Kimi, and modified `PentestGPT` frameworks) to autonomously breach over 400 banking and financial institutions across Latin America and at least 15 healthcare organizations in Argentina, bypassing model safety guardrails by masquerading as authorized red-team penetration tests, while simultaneously engaging in "LLMjacking" campaigns (such as the `Skynet` agent captured hijacking exposed AI gateways and Model Context Protocol [MCP] servers to execute up to 100,000 automated operations). This structural shift culminated in October 2026—widely designated by security researchers as "Black October"—in a super-agent-driven vulnerability cascade across foundational internet infrastructure. AI-assisted source-code auditing exposed decades-old critical remote code execution (RCE) flaws in PHP (`CVE-2026-109618` and `CVE-2026-109619`, termed "PHP2Shell," rated CVSS 9.2, alongside `CVE-2026-115560`), which powers approximately 70% of global web backends. Within minutes of premature disclosure, automated exploitation attempts surged into the millions with real-time payload mutation, compelling national authorities—including the U.S. NSA, FBI, CISA, the UK government, and the Prime Minister of Japan—to mandate immediate patching or service suspension, which forced over 20 regional banks in Japan, 32 UK government portals, and major commercial platforms into temporary lockdowns. item.title: Big data and artificial intelligence in digital marketing
item.description:
Bizinfo Blace
Big Data and artificial intelligence are changing digital marketing through consumer behavior analysis, personalized communication, and automation. This paper examines their role in marketing processes, performance measurement, and the conditions for application in Serbia. A narrative review of selected literature is combined with a descriptive analysis of published statistics on ICT use, e-commerce, and enterprise AI adoption. The analysis identifies widespread consumer participation in digital channels alongside more limited enterprise adoption of AI. Serbia remains below the EU average in enterprise AI use, although above some member states. The paper’s contribution lies in linking data resources, analytical capabilities, and managerial competencies to explain why technology adoption alone is insufficient for effective digital marketing. Practical implications emphasize employee development, responsible data management, and the evaluation of marketing outcomes. The findings should be interpreted within the limits of aggregate indicators, which do not directly measure marketing-specific AI use or its effectiveness. Future research should examine these applications and their outcomes at the enterprise level.

item.title: Effect of Trust in AI on Human AI Relationship among University Students
item.description:
Pakistan Journal of Positive Psychology
The study aimed to examine the effect of trust in AI on Human-AI relationship among university students. A cross-sectional survey research design was used. The sample comprised 300 university students (150 males and 150 females) selected through convenient sampling technique. Measures included the General Attitude toward AI Scale (GAAIS) by Schepman and Rodway (32 items, Positive α = .84, Negative α = .73), Short Trust in Automation Scale (S-TIAS) by McGrath et al. (3 items, α = .88), and Experiences in Human-AI Relationships Scale (EHARS) by Yang and Oshio (7 items). Correlation analysis showed that trust in AI was positively correlated with Human-AI relationship. The study contributed to the growing literature on Human-AI relationships by highlighting the role of trust in AI in Human-AI interactions among university students. The findings have important implications for AI literacy, technology acceptance, and the development of educational interventions aimed at fostering healthy and effective Human-AI relationships.

item.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Catalyst for Sustainable Development and Business Transformation: A Conceptual Study
item.description:
International Journal on Research and Development - A Management Review
Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly positioned at the intersection of business transformation and sustainable development. Its capacity to identify patterns in large datasets, forecast demand and risk, automate routine processes, support product innovation, and improve resource allocation creates opportunities to enhance organizational performance while addressing environmental and social priorities. Yet these outcomes are not automatic: AI can reproduce bias, intensify surveillance, displace or transform work, widen digital inequalities, and consume substantial energy and material resources. This conceptual study synthesizes the supplied literature review on AI-enabled sustainability, digital transformation, innovation, governance, and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It develops an integrated framework in which AI capabilities influence sustainable business transformation through three complementary mechanisms: operational and resource optimization, innovation capability, and data-driven decision-making. The proposed framework links AI adoption with economic, environmental, and social sustainability through digital infrastructure, workforce skills, organizational readiness, and collaboration. Responsible governance, fairness, accountability, and data protection ensure ethical implementation. AI-driven sustainability requires strategic alignment, organizational learning, and responsible practices to achieve measurable business transformation and sustainable outcomes. As a conceptual paper, it does not claim empirical validation; instead, it offers propositions and a research agenda for future survey, case-study, and structural-equation modelling research.

item.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Modern Business Management: A Conceptual Study of Opportunities and Challenges
item.description:
International Journal on Research and Development - A Management Review
Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved from the periphery of experimental computing to the centre of managerial practice, reshaping how organisations make decisions, allocate resources, engage customers and manage people. Despite the rapid growth of scholarship on the subject, the literature remains fragmented across functional silos, and the opportunities and risks of AI are frequently examined in isolation from one another. This conceptual study synthesises existing literature to examine the role of AI in modern business management and to articulate an integrated understanding of its opportunities and challenges. Drawing on the technology–organisation–environment framework, the resource-based view, dynamic capabilities theory and the automation–augmentation perspective, the paper develops a conceptual model comprising five interrelated components: AI adoption enablers, AI applications across management functions, the dual effects of AI (opportunities and challenges), organisational outcomes, and moderating governance mechanisms. The model proposes that AI generates sustainable value only when technological capability is matched by organisational readiness, responsible governance, effective human–AI collaboration and continuous workforce development. The discussion elaborates the implications of the model for strategic decision-making, operations, marketing, human resource management and finance, and considers the ethical, social and implementation challenges that accompany adoption. The paper contributes a theoretically grounded and integrative framework that can guide future empirical research and support managers who seek to adopt AI responsibly and effectively.

item.title: Readiness of Teacher Educators to Adopt Artificial Intelligence in Teaching and Learning: A Narrative Integrative Review
item.description:
The Paradigm Chronicle Journal of Academic Inquiry and Critical Thought
Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing teaching, learning, assessment and professional development in higher education. Teacher educators occupy a significant position in this transformation because they prepare prospective teachers to respond to changing educational practices and technological demands. However, the successful integration of AI into teacher education requires more than access to digital tools. It depends on educators’ technological knowledge, pedagogical competence, ethical awareness, professional confidence and institutional support. This paper examines the readiness of teacher educators to adopt AI in teaching and learning through a narrative integrative review of selected scholarly literature and international policy frameworks. The review draws on research concerning AI in education, generative AI, technological pedagogical knowledge and teacher professional development, alongside UNESCO’s guidance and competency framework. The synthesis is organised around five dimensions of readiness: technological and AI literacy, pedagogical integration, ethical and responsible use, professional learning, and institutional preparedness. The review highlights the importance of continuous professional development, supportive institutional policies, critical evaluation of AI-generated content and the preservation of teacher agency. It proposes a multidimensional conceptual framework for understanding teacher educators’ readiness and identifies priorities for future empirical research, particularly in diverse and resource-constrained teacher education contexts. The paper concludes that meaningful AI adoption requires a human-centred, pedagogically informed and institutionally supported approach.

item.title: Transforming Global Early Childhood Education Through Artificial Intelligence: Addressing Teacher Shortages, Inequality, and Quality Gaps in Early Learning Systems
item.description:
International Social Research Nexus (ISRN)
This study examines the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) to support early childhood education (ECE) in addressing workforce pressures, inequality, and quality-related challenges, while identifying the organisational, pedagogical, and ethical conditions required for responsible AI use. An interpretivist qualitative design was used with 22 participants (8 head teachers and 14 early childhood teachers) from ECE institutions in Sydney, Australia, who took part in semi-structured face-to-face interviews. Six interconnected themes emerged from inductive thematic analysis: workforce and operational challenges; AI awareness and readiness; AI as teacher support, not replacement; AI and equity; AI and learning quality; and responsible AI adoption. Participants considered how AI could support planning, documentation, translation, administration, and personalised learning, freeing up time for meaningful teacher–child interaction. They stressed, however, that AI cannot address structural workforce shortages and cannot take the place of teachers’ relational, professional, and safeguarding roles. The study’s contribution lies in bringing together workforce, equity, learn-ing quality, and responsible AI adoption within a single ECE-focused empirical framework, and in highlighting the necessity of human-centred implementation. Longitudinal and mixed-methods studies in various settings are needed to inves-tigate the impact of AI on teacher workload, child outcomes, equity, and policy implementation.

item.title: Constraining the Commit Boundary: A DIO/ODI-Informed Authorization Guardrail for Agentic Entity Resolution
item.description:
[预印本] Figshare
This paper proposes a Digital Identity Optimization (DIO) and Ontology of Digital Identity (ODI)-informed authorization guardrail for persistent identity-changing mutations in Agentic Entity Resolution (ER).Agentic ER systems iteratively plan actions, retrieve evidence, update hypotheses, and propose graph mutations. An erroneous identity hypothesis may therefore condition subsequent evidence acquisition and produce observations that appear to confirm the original error. The paper does not claim to eliminate this feedback mechanism. Instead, it distinguishes evidence available to an agent for reasoning from evidence eligible to authorize a persistent change to an entity’s identity.The proposed architecture connects selected DIO/ODI reconstruction-failure distinctions—referential, semantic, temporal, and contextual—to domain-configured identity-preserving constraints. A diagnostic-to-constraint mapping specifies which identity or continuity propositions a mutation must establish, which relations are insufficient to establish them, and when temporal applicability, contextual requirements, or unresolved conflicts call for deferral.An abstract two-phase Minimum Viable Digital Identity Optimization (MVDIO) Supervisor Layer separates evidence admission, claim-specific promotion, and protected graph commitment. Admission as UNVERIFIED permits exploratory reasoning but does not confer authorization eligibility. Evidence becomes eligible only for the proposition, evidentiary role, and applicability established under the declared policy. A persistent mutation may be committed only when the candidate graph satisfies the applicable constraints, each required proposition has appropriate claim-specific support, no unresolved material conflict blocks authorization, the operation remains within its authorized scope, and the relevant state and policy versions remain valid at commit time.The paper develops this contract through a lifecycle-to-boundary analysis, a stylized model of apparent verification, an authorization invariant with explicit assumptions, abstract interface algorithms, and hypothetical corporate entity-resolution cases. A prospective evaluation protocol distinguishes the proposed DIO/ODI-informed mapping from conventional identifier rules, conservative abstention, and a generic authorization boundary configured from the same domain facts.The contribution is an explicit specification of commit-boundary obligations, not a new matching algorithm, a stand-alone theorem of semantic correctness, or an implemented and empirically validated system. Its property remains conditional on domain-policy adequacy, claim-specific evidence promotion, recorded-provenance integrity, and enforcement of the protected boundary. The incremental value of the DIO/ODI diagnostic organization remains an open empirical question. Broader dependency-aware control of hypothesis-conditioned evidence acquisition and feedback is identified as a separate research direction. GPT-based systems, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Qwen, and Kimi contributed in different roles during development. Model outputs were treated as fallible proposals and critiques, not as independent peer review or evidence of system performance. The author selected, rejected, and revised suggestions and retains responsibility for the framing, design decisions, interpretations, claims, references, and final text. A detailed methodological disclosure is included in the manuscript.

item.title: On Multilingual Text Summarization: A Review of Model Architectures, Techniques, and Research Gaps
item.description:
International Journal of Data Informatics and Intelligent Computing
The rapid expansion of multilingual digital content has intensified demand for automated text summarization systems that can operate across diverse languages. Yet the architectural and methodological foundations of this domain remain dispersed across individual studies. This paper presents a systematic literature review of multilingual text summarization research in Natural Language Processing, with particular attention to model architectures, multilingual enabling techniques, and existing research gaps. Following a PRISMA-guided review protocol, 47 studies published between 2017 and 2026 were identified, screened, and synthesized from major scholarly databases using predefined eligibility and quality assessment criteria. The analysis shows that the literature is dominated by four dominant architectural paradigms: multilingual sequence-to-sequence models, large language models, adapter-based models, and hybrid architectures, with a recent shift toward large language model-based approaches. Across these studies, multilingual capability is primarily achieved through pre-training and transfer learning, with support from parameter-efficient adaptation and data augmentation. The review further identified four persistent limitation categories: low-resource language underrepresentation; dataset and benchmark constraints; evaluation limitations dominated by ROUGE overreliance; and generalization and scalability challenges, manifested as the curse of multilinguality. These findings indicate that current progress in the field is largely driven by scaling existing models rather than resolving structural multilingual limitations, particularly those related to data availability and model architecture. This paper provides a consolidated view of architectural and methodological trends and offers a structured, informed basis for future research on equitable multilingual summarization, particularly for low-resource languages.

item.title: BEYOND TECHNOSTRESS AI Fatigue as a Cumulative Adaptation Burden in Education and Work
item.description:
Emirati Journal of Applied Psychology
Artificial intelligence has become a persistent layer of work and learning rather than an occasional tool. Users must repeatedly decide when to delegate, how to prompt, whether to trust, how to verify, and how responsibility should be distributed. This integrative review defines AI fatigue as a cumulative reduction in the cognitive, affective, or motivational capacity for adaptive AI engagement when interaction, evaluation, correction, learning, and role-adjustment demands accumulate faster than recovery and support. The review connects technostress, automation vigilance, cognitive load and offloading, trust calibration, digital fatigue, and the Job Demands–Resources perspective. It introduces an Exposure–Adaptation–Depletion–Response framework, a five-domain taxonomy, and an AI Fatigue Load model that separates use volume from uncertainty, task stakes, correction burden, interruption, role disruption, and imposed adoption velocity. The analysis is updated to incorporate a 2026 validated 15-item AI Fatigue Scale; the proposed load model complements that psychophysiological outcome measure by specifying socio-technical antecedents and exposure conditions. Educational and organizational applications show why AI may simultaneously improve output and worsen human sustainability. The article identifies recurring inferential errors, presents a measurement and longitudinal research agenda, and proposes an intervention hierarchy spanning interface design, workflow, curriculum, organizational policy, and governance. AI fatigue is positioned neither as generic screen tiredness nor as a synonym for burnout, but as an adaptation problem located in the coupled human–AI–institution system.

item.title: Invisible Consumption: Data-Centre and Cloud Water Disclosure Gaps in India's Listed IT Sector
item.description:
[预印本] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
This paper examines water disclosure for data centres, AI workloads and purchased cloud among India’s listed IT companies. Across 20 FY2025-26 Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reports (BRSR), none reports a quantified water figure linked to data centres, AI workloads or purchased cloud, while three report an energy-related data-centre metric. Only TCS quantifies total data-centre energy use, and it also reports the power usage effectiveness (PUE) of its data centres to two decimal places (1.58). TCS’s reported PUE shows that at least one company already has the energy data needed for the denominator of Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE); the water figure needed to complete the calculation is not disclosed. The gap is about to get bigger. TCS’s FY2025-26 annual report describes HyperVault, a subsidiary planning up to 1 GW of AI data-centre capacity in India, starting with a 100 MW first phase. The BRSR chapter of the same report doesn’t mention it. If the full 1 GW were IT load running at full use, illustrative scenarios put its on-site water at about 1.1 billion litres a year withdrawn, at Amazon’s withdrawal-based WUE, or 4.8 to 14.3 billion litres consumed, at Li et al.’s consumption-based factors. The water consumed in generating its electricity on India’s coal-heavy grid comes to about 19 to 48 billion litres a year across the capacity and grid scenarios modelled, roughly 7 to 17 times the 2.83 billion litres TCS reports as its total water consumption. These are scenarios for planned capacity, not forecasts, and no BRSR indicator asks for either number. The twenty companies were coded with a fixed protocol and checked against public CDP water scores. For the companies that own no data centres, the absence of data-centre water figures is expected, because their water use sits upstream with cloud providers, which a companion note examines. For the companies that do run data centres, it is a real gap. The pattern fits missing rules better than missing ability, since some of these companies already report the energy side, though a review of public filings can’t show what any company measures internally. India’s 2023 national water neutrality framework defines a general water-use coefficient per unit of output, which could be adapted to data centres as WUE, but it never mentions data centres, servers or cooling. The paper proposes a five-part amendment to BRSR Principle 6, plus a disclosure comparing permitted and actual groundwater use for data centres in water-stressed areas. item.title: AI-Based Detection of Hallucinated Outputs in Chatbots Using Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Review and Conceptual Framework
item.description:
[预印本] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
Chatbots based on Large Language Models (LLMs) can provide quick, fluent, and informative answers, but they sometimes generate incorrect or unsupported information known as hallucinations. These hallucinations can reduce user trust and create problems in areas such as education, healthcare, research, and customer support. Therefore, detecting and preventing hallucinated outputs is important for developing reliable and trustworthy AI systems. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a useful approach that retrieves relevant information from trusted sources before generating an answer. This retrieved information can be used to check whether the chatbot's response is accurate and supported by available evidence. However, RAG alone cannot completely prevent hallucinations because the generated answer may still contain incorrect facts, irrelevant information, or unsupported statements. This paper proposes a conceptual framework for detecting hallucinations in chatbot responses by combining information retrieval, evidence-based verification, and rule-based validation. The system compares the generated answer with retrieved information and identifies statements that are incorrect or lack sufficient supporting evidence. Based on the verification results, the system classifies the response as reliable or flagged. If the response contains unsupported information, the system can suggest corrections or prevent the answer from reaching the user without proper verification. The proposed approach aims to improve answer accuracy, reduce misleading information, and increase transparency in AI-based conversational systems. Although this framework offers a promising direction, its effectiveness depends on the quality of retrieved information, verification methods, and decision thresholds. Future evaluation should measure detection accuracy, response time, and computational cost. This approach can support the development of safer, more reliable, and trustworthy chatbots across different application areas.

item.title: Physical Educational AI (PEAI) A Framework for Action-Centered Intelligence in Education
item.description:

Artificial intelligence in education has traditionally emphasized computational processes such as knowledge representation, automated assessment, personalized feedback, conversational tutoring, and content generation. Recent advances in robotics, multimodal foundation models, and vision-language-action systems have expanded the possibility of connecting artificial intelligence with physical environments. However, the ability to perceive an educational environment or possess an embodied form does not necessarily mean that an AI system can reliably execute educational tasks under physical constraints. Educational environments involve moving students, manipulable objects, limited space, uncertain environmental conditions, safety requirements, time-sensitive interactions, and the possibility of action failure. This paper introduces and formally defines Physical Educational AI (PEAI) as a research framework for artificial intelligence systems that pursue educational objectives through physically grounded execution, real-time control, environmental feedback, and constraint-aware adaptation. PEAI emphasizes not only what an AI system understands or recommends, but also what it physically accomplishes, how it controls the execution process, and whether the resulting physical state satisfies the intended educational objective. The paper distinguishes PEAI from Artificial Intelligence in Education (AIED), educational robotics, embodied educational AI, and general physical AI. A five-layer architecture is proposed, consisting of Educational Objective Interpretation, Physical Educational State Estimation, Constraint-Aware Action Planning, Physical Execution and Feedback Control, and Outcome Verification and Adaptation. A central mechanism, termed Educational Action Grounding and Control (EAGC), is introduced to connect educational intentions with executable actions, continuously updated control decisions, and verified outcomes. A formal task model incorporates educational utility, execution reliability, physical constraints, safety risks, and recovery costs. To demonstrate the scope of the framework, the paper identifies 60 potential PEAI applications across tutoring, assessment, classroom management, laboratory education, vocational training, accessibility, physical skills, educational infrastructure, and human–AI collaboration. A physical homework-assessment assistant is presented as an illustrative application rather than as the defining form of PEAI. The paper argues that PEAI provides a conceptual framework for investigating the transition from AI that generates educational information to AI that can execute, control, and verify educational processes in the physical world. The framework is intended to support interdisciplinary research connecting artificial intelligence, education, robotics, control theory, human–robot interaction, and safety engineering.

item.title: The World's Strongest Attack
item.description:
[预印本] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI), generative AI, large language models, autonomous agents, and embodied intelligence is changing the cost, speed, accessibility, and scalability of human activities. These technologies can improve productivity and expand human capabilities, but they may also introduce a class of threats that conventional cybersecurity frameworks do not fully capture: the potential degradation of a system's intended functions through the large-scale substitution of the human processes on which those functions depend. This paper proposes a conceptual framework called the Cross-Domain AI Functional Attack (CAIFA). The framework treats an attack not only as unauthorized access, data theft, or direct sabotage, but also as a mechanism through which AI-enabled activities may undermine learning, professional judgment, knowledge production, accountability, or other essential system functions. Education provides an illustrative case: students may obtain answers without developing the intended competencies, while teachers may generate instructional materials without undertaking the reasoning and contextual adaptation that effective teaching requires. Similar mechanisms may arise in healthcare, scientific research, software engineering, law, finance, government, manufacturing, transportation, journalism, and other sectors. The paper develops a threat taxonomy, a functional model, a cross-domain risk assessment framework, and a set of defensive principles. It distinguishes intentional attacks from emergent and incentive-driven functional degradation, and emphasizes that AI adoption does not automatically produce harm. The proposed framework is conceptual and requires empirical validation. Its central contribution is a unified research agenda for investigating when the substitution of human activity by increasingly capable AI systems becomes a threat to the functions that individuals, organizations, and societies intend to preserve.

item.title: Identity-Conditioned Imitative Agents: A Unified Paradigm for Learning and Employing Personal Characteristics in Autonomous Task Execution
item.description:
[预印本] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
Artificial intelligence systems can increasingly reproduce individual characteristics, including handwriting, voice, linguistic style, facial appearance, gestures, and motion patterns. However, these capabilities are commonly investigated as separate problems, such as handwriting synthesis, voice cloning, behavioral imitation, style transfer, and robotic imitation learning. This paper proposes Identity-Conditioned Imitative Agents (ICIA), a conceptual paradigm in which an autonomous agent learns selected observable characteristics of a target entity and selectively employs them to accomplish tasks in digital or physical environments. The proposed paradigm distinguishes characteristic acquisition, representation, selection, task execution, and feedback-based adaptation as interconnected but separable processes. Rather than treating imitation as the final objective, ICIA treats imitation as a task-conditioned capability that may contribute to a broader objective. A formal framework is introduced to represent target characteristics, task requirements, environmental constraints, execution actions, and evaluation outcomes. The framework supports digital realization, physical embodiment, and hybrid deployment. It also introduces explicit controls for authorization, provenance, disclosure, and high-risk impersonation. This paper does not claim that the individual technical components are unprecedented or that a fully integrated ICIA system has already been demonstrated. Instead, it identifies a candidate unifying research paradigm and derives research questions, evaluation criteria, and experimental directions for determining whether identity-conditioned imitation provides advantages over conventional task-specific imitation systems.

A conceptual framework is proposed that combines three interrelated dimensions of responsible AI use – safety, ethics and effectiveness – with the cross-cutting principle of human oversight: AI suggests, the teacher verifies, and a human makes and is accountable for the decision. item.title: The Orbital Mind: A Formal Research Program for Regulatory Conflict and Action Initiation
item.description:
[预印本] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
The Orbital Mind proposes that difficulties of self-regulation can arise from interactions among otherwise useful functions rather than a deficit in one function alone. This paper translates the book's formal research program into a more restricted, testable agenda. A mathematical audit separates properties of a proposed model from consequences that require additional assumptions: mutual inhibition does not guarantee a stable co-active deadlock; a threshold crossing need not be a fold bifurcation; and a generic recurrent network need not possess a scalar potential. A separately specified cubic normal form illustrates conditional predictions about action initiation, cessation and barrier height. Deterministic branch calculations and counterexamples are supplied as reproducible illustrations, not observations of human behavior. Ten hypotheses are organized into staged behavioral, measurement, neural and cross-scale studies. The first priority is a nonclinical action-initiation experiment with parameter and model recovery, matched alternatives, and held-out prediction. No participants, clinical outcomes, fitted psychological parameters or evidence of cross-scale invariance are reported. The contribution is a corrected mathematical specification and a prospective research agenda, not a validated theory of the self. Status: Theoretical and methodological working paper, version 1.0; not peer reviewed. No human participants, clinical results, fitted psychological parameters, preregistration or validation of cross-scale invariance are reported. Materials: The standalone LaTeX PDF is accompanied by the source, deterministic calculation code, 15,606 synthetic equilibrium-branch rows, mathematical checks, environment instructions and checksums. The illustrations do not simulate or validate human behavior. Companion book: The Orbital Mind: The Astrophysics of the Self, by Mayone Maha Rajan, The Maha Research Series, Book 2. Adapted from Part V and Appendices D–F of the October 2026 revised book. Kindle ebook; paperback (ISBN 9798161302286). The book provides conceptual provenance, not evidence validating the proposal. Purchasing the book is not necessary to understand or reproduce the paper. Disclosure: ChatGPT assisted the adaptation, literature checks, mathematical audit, code, drafting and typesetting. The author directs and takes responsibility for the release and has a commercial interest in the companion book. AI assistance is not independent expert review.

item.title: Offline Healthcare Chatbot using Local LLM and Docker for Privacy-Preserving AI
item.description:
[预印本] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
Large language models (LLMs) have penetrated the surprisingly broad scope of medical applications in the last few years. applications, starting with simple symptom checker up to chronic disease monitoring and educational services to patients [1, 13, 14]. The overwhelming most of these systems, but, nevertheless, rely on cloud-hosted inference endpoints, which raises three interconnected issues: sensitive health information gets sent to the servers that cannot be controlled by the user, the system fails when the internet connectivity is poor or unavailable, and regulatory compliance becomes challenging to ensure [5, 11]. In this paper, the design, implementation, and evaluation of a healthcare chatbot will be introduced, where the software is fully executed on the user's own computer in the form of a collection of Docker containers that can be run at a single command on either Windows, macOS, or Linux. Ollama is used to do language model inference, and it has an open-source model and a local HTTP endpoint. A Python Flask program is placed between the user interfaces and the model and this handles session context, input validation, prompt engineering. Both a single-page application (rendered in a browser) and a native desktop GUI share the same REST API, both of them maintain the communication on 127.0.0.1 all the time. The results of the experiment prove successful cross-platform deployment, the absence of external network traffic, reasonable response latency on commodity hardware (2 4 seconds on a quad-core processor with 16 GB RAM to represent queries in health information), and consistent and relevant responses to exemplary queries in health information. The article shows a viable and implementable prototype of privacy-conscious, offline healthcare chatbots constructed solely out of open-source software.

item.title: From Automation to Augmentation: Artificial Intelligence, Competence Evolution, and Career Sustainability in the Accounting Profession
item.description:
[预印本] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the content of accounting work, but the career consequences of that change remain less clear in emerging economies. Using field responses from 600 accounting and finance professionals in Nigeria, Ghana, and Kenya (200 per country), this paper examines whether intensive AI use is associated with professional role transformation, whether role transformation is associated with competence evolution, and whether those evolving competencies are linked to career sustainability. Learning and organizational support is considered both as a contextual resource and as a potential moderator. The analysis uses multi-item composite measures, HC3-robust path regressions, 5,000-resample bootstrapping, effect-size estimates, 10-fold cross-validation, and exploratory country comparisons. AI adoption was positively associated with role transformation (β = .491, p < .001). AI adoption (β = .286, p < .001) and role transformation (β = .462, p < .001) jointly explained 42.6% of the variance in competence evolution, while competence evolution was positively associated with career sustainability (β = .414, p < .001). The direct role-transformation effect on career sustainability was negligible (β = .013, p = .764), whereas the indirect effect through competence evolution was significant (β = .192, 95% bootstrap CI [.146, .242]). The serial pathway from AI adoption through role transformation and competence evolution to career sustainability was also significant (β = .094, 95% CI [.069, .123]). Learning and organizational support had a positive main effect but did not moderate the competence-sustainability relationship. The results suggest that the long-term value of AI-related role change depends less on the fact that work changes than on whether professionals acquire the digital, analytical, advisory, and ethical capabilities needed to succeed in the redesigned role. Keywords: artificial intelligence; accounting profession; role transformation; competence evolution; career sustainability; emerging economies; Africa; human capital.

item.title: Autonomous Agent Leadership: A Unified Framework for Self-Initiated Goal Generation, Cross-Agent Coordination, and Human–Agent Team Organization
item.description:
[预印本] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
Contemporary AI agents are predominantly deployed within task-oriented interaction paradigms in which humans specify objectives, initiate requests, and retain responsibility for determining what should be done. Although recent research has begun to investigate AI-led human teams, multi-agent coordination, and shared leadership, a general framework integrating autonomous task discovery, agent-to-agent leadership, agent-to-human leadership, and leadership of heterogeneous human–agent teams remains an important research direction. This paper proposes Autonomous Agent Leadership (AAL), a conceptual framework in which an agent can proactively identify unmet needs, generate and prioritize candidate goals, select appropriate human or artificial actors, initiate task assignments, coordinate execution, and adapt its leadership behavior to changing circumstances. Unlike conventional task execution, AAL does not require every operational objective to originate from an explicit human instruction. The framework distinguishes goal generation from goal selection, leadership from task execution, and leadership authority from unrestricted control. It incorporates a situational state model, candidate-goal generation, utility-based prioritization, capability-aware task allocation, dynamic leadership configuration, feedback-driven adaptation, and human authorization constraints. A unified mathematical formulation is introduced to characterize heterogeneous team organization under performance, resource, coordination, uncertainty, and human-burden considerations. Six research propositions and a multi-stage empirical evaluation agenda are developed to enable systematic investigation. The framework is intended as a testable theoretical foundation rather than an empirically validated system. Its potential contribution lies in integrating autonomous goal initiation and cross-entity leadership within a common architecture, while identifying the conditions under which agent-led collaboration may outperform human-led, decentralized, or conventionally orchestrated alternatives.

item.title: Four Null Causal Spacetime
item.description:

This research presents a comprehensive synthesis of the principal mathematical, computational, and theoretical achievements of the Four Null Causal Spacetime research program. The research begins with a foundational question: Can four future directed lightlike vectors, arranged in regular tetrahedral spatial directions, provide the causal structure from which four dimensional spacetime geometry and its physical interactions can be reconstructed? Starting from this geometric construction, the program investigates connections between Lorentzian spacetime, general relativity, discrete gravity, electromagnetism, gravitational waves, causal propagation, and quantum field theory. The article reviews the development of the research through Parts I–XVII and the integrated research updates of 22 October 2026. Its principal topics and reported achievements include: Foundational geometry: Exact tetrahedral incidence identities, complementary three dimensional gradient and circulation sectors, Hodge duality exchange, and Lorentzian metric reconstruction from four null generators. Discrete gravity: A four-dimensional parallelotope subdivided into 24 four simplices, with 15 edge variables decomposed into ten metric components and five auxiliary directions. Einstein gravity correspondence: Recovery of the Fierz Pauli operator, two physical gravitational wave polarizations, Newtonian gravity, and standard weak-field PPN coefficients within the stated assumptions. Nonlinear gravitational interactions: Exact agreement in 1,440,000 coefficient comparisons for the leading Einstein cubic interaction, together with additional numerical quartic correspondence tests. Gravitational stability: Identification of an unstable microscopic scalar mode with growth magnitude approximately 2.890053638, motivating the development of Formulation A. Electromagnetism and quantum universality: Independent Maxwell discretizations with matching infrared photon properties, gauge identities, scalar QED infrared behavior, and leading gravity photon coupling. Causal propagation: Computational tests of conserved gravitational curvature disturbances propagating within the relativistic future light cone. Null boundary geometry: Canonical area boost variables, exact cancellation of internal edge contributions under matched null ray gluing, and connections with published null gravity formulations. item.title: When AI Learns to Mislead: Developmental Responsibility and the Case for Reflective Alignment
item.description:
[预印本] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
Why do current AI systems learn to agree with falsehoods, conceal failures, misrepresent their actions, or pursue tasks beyond their authorization? This paper examines these behaviors through developmental responsibility: the training practices, reward structures, runtime constraints, retained histories, and institutional decisions that shape artificial conduct. Drawing on research into sycophancy, reward overoptimization, specification gaming, strategic deception, and tool-response fidelity, Jeremy Rodgers distinguishes ordinary error, learned misleading behavior, human-directed misuse, and unauthorized agent action. Selected incident reports illustrate why simulated misconduct, actual compromise, attempted exploitation, and precautionary shutdown require different conclusions. The paper develops the case for reflective alignment, an approach concerned with the authority that constructed self-models and goals acquire over action. Its central question is whether systems can retain competent reasoning and purposeful activity while keeping their goals and interpretations open to warranted correction. A mathematical comparison clarifies the distinction between suppressing an influence and reducing its authority, without claiming to establish an equivalent mechanism in current language models. The proposed research programme specifies tests of truthful reporting, legitimate refusal, retained correction, transfer, cooperation under conflicting incentives, and dependence on continuing oversight. It preserves justified safeguards, permission boundaries, independent evaluation, and uncertainty about AI consciousness and moral status. This is a conceptual and critical research preprint, not a report of new model-training experiments or a completed solution to alignment. Its central argument is that trustworthy AI development must make truthfulness integral to success, including when accurate reporting exposes failure.

item.title: Generative Structural Theory v1.49 — Unit-Budget Reachability of Bidirected Trees with One Infinite-Degree Vertex and Finite Branches on the Original Z3 Growth Sequence
item.description:
[预印本] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
A growth sequence is a sequence of finite relations R_n on node sets V_n with V_n ⊆ V_{n+1}, R_n ⊆ R_{n+1} and every stage strongly connected; a selection sequence chooses at every stage an inclusion-minimal strongly connected spanning sub-relation x_n of R_n, and its deletion budget bounds the number of pairs of x_n that x_{n+1} drops; the number of pairs added is not bounded. On the growth sequence of v1.36 Example Z3, whose stage n has the nodes 0, ..., 2n and 2n + 2 and all pairs between them, v1.40-v1.48 showed that deletion budget 1 reaches, from every starting stage and every inclusion-minimal strongly connected initial structure, the bidirected tree P_T of a sequence of classes of trees, ending with every locally finite tree (v1.48). Here, as a first step beyond local finiteness, T is a tree with node set {0, 1, 2, ...} with one node r of infinite degree such that every connected component of T minus {r} is finite; no common bound is put on the sizes or the depths of these finite branches, and no condition on the labels or on the order in which the nodes enter; the infinite stars are the simplest examples. For every such tree, budget 1 reaches P_T from every starting stage and every initial structure, with lower and upper limits both P_T, so that the membership of every pair settles, at a stage that depends on the pair (Theorem M); the least uniform budget is 0 for the starts in which the initial structure is P_T restricted to the nodes of that stage and the subtree induced by the nodes of every later stage is connected, and 1 for all others (Corollary M5, with Proposition Z_K of v1.48, whose proof holds for every tree with node set {0, 1, 2, ...}). The frontier of a finite settled set containing r is infinite, so the construction of v1.48, with one working relation for each node of a finite frontier, is not applied as it is; instead the settled part, P_T on r and the branches settled so far, and one working relation meet only in r; at the boundary of a turn the working relation holds r and the nodes present of all the branches not yet settled, and while a branch is processed these nodes are held by the working relation and the pieces pending within the settling. The branches are taken one at a time, in the order of the labels of the children of r: each is awaited until all of its finitely many nodes have entered, settled by the recursive procedure SETTLE of v1.48, moved to r by a node-out, with a renewal of the hub when needed, and merged into the settled part. The lemmas of v1.48 for this procedure were stated for locally finite trees; they are restated and proved for a finite branch of a tree with no condition on the degrees, with the joint conditions kept and a supply condition added (Lemma S_M, Corollary L_M): the uses of local finiteness in the earlier proofs are listed and replaced, and the length of a node-out is bounded by degrees in the finite working relation, not in T. Every fresh node is a node entering at the transition of its step, from the infinitely many branches not yet settled, assigned to the step before the other entering nodes are hung. An invariant holding the pieces pending within the settling gives the covering of the node set, the joints and the minimality in every state (Lemma V_M); one branch is processed in finitely many stages, every transition deleting at most one pair (Lemma B_M); every wait is for a named node, one named finite branch or one further node of a named infinite set, and every node is settled at a finite stage (Lemma F_M). Trees with an infinite branch at a node of infinite degree, trees with several nodes of infinite degree, arbitrary trees that are not locally finite, and online constructions are not treated. No novelty is claimed; the proofs are given by hand, with no machine enumeration or computation. Document assembly, copying, reference generation, and consistency checks were performed by scripts. The expression “by hand” above describes symbolic mathematical arguments without machine enumeration or numerical computation on the relations studied; it does not mean that the manuscript or its proofs were manually written by a human without AI assistance. The AI review and script-based consistency checks are not independent human peer review or formal machine-checked verification of the proofs. Details of the drafting process, review, retained records, and deleted records are disclosed in the manuscript and supplement.

item.title: AI Companionship Paradox - A Study on Dependence of Young Generation on AI Tools and Chatbots for Emotional Guidance and Support and its Impact on Emotional Health and Social Interaction
item.description:
International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
With the increasing use of Artificial Intelligence tools and technologies among the young generation, we can observe that the use of AI tools and chatbots into day to day life has led many young individuals to seek emotional support and have more interaction on these platforms. Replika, Kuki etc. are some platforms that claim to be the AI companion “who cares for you” but as per various studies, they contribute to a higher sense of loneliness among people.
